programmes.d: The one-of-a-kind Dom DeLuise is Carol's guest for a night of sketches, including a murder investigation invaded by the irrepressible Fireside Girl Alice Portnoy, and a tempestuous "Carol & Sis."

Get ready for the big time as ham actors Funt & Mundane score a hit, leading to a performance at the supersized Astro Bowl. Also: Tim's "Oldest Man" character is completely at sea as a ship's captain.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents The Temptations, Myron Cohen, Vanilla Fudge, Gilbert Price, Jacques D'Amboise, and Allegra Kent.
Acting icon Bruce Dern talks about working with Ann-Margret on Middle Age Crazy, and David Letterman scores laughs describing his visit to a nude beach and his dog’s love life.
Carl Reiner improvises an Italian aria and riffs on ridiculous celebrity stories from the tabloids. Olympic diver Greg Louganis shows off his moves on a trampoline.

programmes.t: Ed Sullivan's Best of Broadway Musicals
programmes.d: A priceless time capsule of TV's golden age, featuring unforgettable performances by legendary Broadway stars and behind-the-scenes interviews with songwriters Rodgers & Hammerstein and Lerner & Loewe. Narrated by the legendary John Raitt.
Don Johnson is a surprise guest in this episode, which also features David Brenner and Dale Robertson.
Lucille Ball and Tim Conway guest star in this hilarious episode, highlighted by a sketch in which Lucy and Carol play rival Rent-A-Car agents vying for Tim's business.
Dick Cavett in jogging shorts? Johnny describes Cavetti’s jitter-calming pre-show run. Cavett tells the story of a guest who died on his show and then…does a magic trick.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Eartha Kitt, Nina Simone, Kalanag, Professor Backwards, Daniele Barioni, and Rodriquez.
Jack Weston and Michele Lee guest star, joining Carol and Harvey for a sketch juxtaposing a bickering married couple and a newly-engaged one. Also: a doctor's visit is an emotional rollercoaster.
Dick Cavett chats about his commencement speech at Yale, (a lot of potty jokes and one-liners, apparently), and his early days as a stand-up comic.
Autograph hounds watch out: Donald Sutherland has a policy on handling signature seekers. Comic actor Martin Mull answers his fan mail and shows off his artwork.
The multitalented Debbie Reynolds and John Davidson guest star in this episode, highlighted by the stirring saga of a squad of World War II nurses: "So Proudly We Heal."
Ed Sullivan presents performances by Sonny & Cher, Tom Jones, Four Tops, The Four Seasons, The Lovin' Spoonful, and Herman's Hermits.
Small screen icon Farrah Fawcett discusses her new TV movie, and Ryan O'Neal is obsessed with her.
Nancy Wilson and Donald O'Connor guest star! Sketches include a housewife plagued by familiar commercials for household products and a loving spoof of the popular "College Musical" subgenre.
Johnny admires Jim Fowler's baby alligator collection, Bob Nelson does stand-up and Teresa Ganzel talks Vegas and Sinatra.
Guest stars Ken Berry and Carl Reiner fly the funny skies in "Disaster '75!" Fasten your seat belts for one of Carol's all-time classic movie spoof sketches that soars on wings of laughter.
Roddy McDowall guest stars! Highlights include Roddy joining "The Family" for a reunion where Mama and the rest are unimpressed by his success, and a "Brief Encounter" with briefer dialogue.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents The Supremes, Gary Lewis and The Playboys, Jan Peerce and Robert Merrill, and The Harlem Globetrotters.
Comic legend Richard Pryor chats about his California-style divorce and SNL alum and movie star Chevy Chase shares the secret behind his famous spot on Gerald Ford impression.
"I saw it in the window, and I just couldn't resist it." One of the show's finest hours, the hilarious spoof "Went With The Wind!" is presented here for your entertainment. Dinah Shore guest stars.
John Larroquette is always a fun guest and for his latest appearance he discusses, hair loss, playing the saxophone, and...The Weasel Awards. Don't ask!
A "Family Show", featuring "The Family"! Ed is going on an out-of-town trip...but Eunice and Mickey want to come along. Elsewhere, Harvey and Carol can't stop making little digs at each other.
Carl Reiner insists that Johnny is a great role model for dating couples. Reflects on shaving his head for a movie, and trades quips on aging with French beauty Catherine Deneuve.
Two of Carol's favorite guest stars, Steve Lawrence and Bernadette Peters, each team up with Carol in another delightful night of comedy.
Two guests for the price of one--Dick Van Dyke and Tony Randall! Sketches include: Dick as a salesman arriving during a couple's quarrel, and Carol and Tony as marrieds with secret hand signals.
Show biz veteran Angie Dickinson talks about men who whistle at women, Tommy Lasorda chats about losing weight, and Dom DeLuise dishes on doing an off-Broadway play with Barbra Streisand.
Jane Connell and the ever-funny Tim Conway guest star! Tonight's episode features Harvey and Tim as tipsy friends coming home from a night of carousing, and a spoof of The Arabian Nights.
Paul Lynde and Peggy Lee are tonight's guests! Along with the usual songs and sketches is an improv comedy performance--and among the performers is a pre-M*A*S*H William Christopher (Father Mulcahy).
Tim Conway and Steve Lawrence guest star! A chimp's bite leads to some monkey business for Tim in one sketch, while another features a business relationship resembling a failed romantic relationship.
Chevy Chase is afraid of snakes and spiders! Plus, John Sutter and Thalassa Cruso stop by and Johnny jokes about a supermarket sushi shoplifter.
Hear what Joan Rivers has to say about retouched magazine covers, Gone With The Wind and Dolly Parton. Plus, Johnny welcomes Japanese TV personality Tetsuko Kuroyanagi.
Guest Stars Mel Torme, Nanette Fabray, and Don Rickles pitch in to help tell "The Tin Pan Alley Story"--with Mel and Carol as songwriting team Potts and Panz on their road to--and from--stardom.
Star party guy, Dean Martin recounts the wild fun celebrating Frank Sinatra’s big 6-0. Also fills in Johnny on playing Las Vegas and his frequent forays into the casinos.
